rv.q: Abounding with witty entertainment and curiosity value, augmented by scene-stealing appearances from two real-life corgis, it confirms the promise shown by Marcelo Dos Santos with his comic monologue
The shift between farce and the more nuanced drama can be jarring. Yet overall Grandage’s production executes itself as nimbly as clockwork, delivering plenty of laughs along with the live corgis.
Wilton and Evans are a delightful duo, bouncing off each other effortlessly.

'Backstairs Billy' is a witty take on the royal household and the goings-on behind the scenes that most people would never be a part of, and the snappy one-liners come thick and fast, but it's all tinged with a hint of sadness, and that's what will stay with you long after the laughter stops.
'Backstairs Billy' really is a great play for a light evening. Something for the heart and soul without being overwhelming or too challenging.

cn.t: Critics find this witty royal household comedy a light, entertaining evening with sharp one-liners and live corgis, though tonal shifts can jar. The blend of laughs and underlying melancholy lingers after curtain call.
